3760050.background: Calgary-Shaw is a suburban south Calgary riding held comfortably by the UCP (Rebecca Schulz won it in 2023). A vacancy triggered a September 14, 2026 by-election. Alberta politics are polarized UCP vs NDP under Naheed Nenshi, with separatist and right-flank parties adding noise. Mike Derry is a listed candidate.

actors.name: United Conservative Party (Danielle Smith)
actors.public: Defends a safe seat; strong suburban Calgary machine and fundraising; has won most recent by-elections in its suburban strongholds.
actors.private: Wants a clean hold to show strength before 2027; worried about vote splitting from separatist or Republican-style right parties and low turnout.

actors.name: Alberta NDP (Naheed Nenshi)
actors.public: Targets Calgary as its growth area; Nenshi popular in the city; will frame by-election as referendum on Smith government.
actors.private: Would treat a close second as success; realistic flip only with major UCP split or scandal.

actors.name: Right-flank / separatist parties
actors.public: Republican or independence-oriented parties field candidates channeling anger at Ottawa and at UCP moderation.
actors.private: Aim to show protest share rather than win; could shave enough UCP votes to make the race close.

actors.name: Calgary-Shaw electorate
actors.public: Suburban, family-oriented, historically conservative; by-election turnout typically low (~30-40%).
actors.private: Likely to default to the UCP absent a strong local grievance or a credible split.

events.name: Major provincial scandal or policy backlash (health, schools, referendum) hits UCP during campaign
Separatist/right-wing candidate polls above 15% in the riding

actors.name: Main challenger(s)
actors.public: Likely current or former councillor running on change, housing, and council dysfunction themes.
actors.private: Need consolidation of anti-incumbent vote; a single strong challenger is far more dangerous than several.

actors.name: Charlottetown voters
actors.public: Small electorate (~30k eligible), modest turnout; typically re-elect incumbents.
actors.private: Discontent on housing and street disorder could make the race competitive if one alternative emerges.

events.name: A strong, well-known single challenger consolidates opposition

actors.name: Neighbourhood/slow-growth bloc
actors.public: Residents' associations opposing rapid densification; can back an alternative candidate.
actors.private: Will support whoever best resists provincial housing mandates; could split or decide outcome.

actors.name: Saanich electorate
